the soils on mine heaps, which are similar in terms of technogenic parent material, climate and soil texture, but differ in the age of pedogenesis, show significant differences in the evolution of soil properties.

soils formed on mining wastes in the Silesia Upland, Poland, have been undergoing pedogenesis for a long time, which resulted in an increase of soil organic matter, aggregate formation, dehydrogense activity, and decrease in Zn Pb and Cd concentrations.

the soils located at the sites of former Zn Pb mining activities in the Silesia Krakow Uplands, southern Poland, are characterized by high contents of Zn, Pb and other heavy metals, but the degree of contamination depends on the duration of pedogenesis.
